title: King of Thieves
statementMd:
*In this problem you will meet the simplified model of game King of Thieves*.

In a new ZeptoLab game called "King of Thieves" your aim is to reach a chest with gold by controlling your character, avoiding traps and obstacles on your way.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/89ecf94723f2c4b2bbb4ab5e555fd8fca72cbcde.png)

An interesting feature of the game is that you can design your own levels that will be available to other players. Let's consider the following simple design of a level.

A dungeon consists of $*n*$ segments located at a same vertical level, each segment is either a platform that character can stand on, or a pit with a trap that makes player lose if he falls into it. All segments have the same length, platforms on the scheme of the level are represented as `'*'` and pits are represented as `'.'`.

One of things that affects speedrun characteristics of the level is a possibility to perform a series of consecutive jumps of the same length. More formally, when the character is on the platform number $*i*_{1}$, he can make a sequence of jumps through the platforms $*i*_{1} < *i*_{2} < ... < *i*_{*k*}$, if $*i*_{2} - *i*_{1} = *i*_{3} - *i*_{2} = ... = *i*_{*k*} - *i*_{*k* - 1}$. Of course, all segments $*i*_{1}, *i*_{2}, ... *i*_{*k*}$ should be exactly the platforms, not pits.

Let's call a level to be *good* if you can perform a sequence of **four** jumps of the same length or in the other words there must be a sequence $*i*_{1}, *i*_{2}, ..., *i*_{5}$, consisting of **five** platforms so that the intervals between consecutive platforms are of the same length. Given the scheme of the level, check if it is good.

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$) — the number of segments on the level.

Next line contains the scheme of the level represented as a string of $*n*$ characters `'*'` and `'.'`.

## Output

If the level is *good*, print the word `"yes"` (without the quotes), otherwise print the word `"no"` (without the quotes).

## Note

In the first sample test you may perform a sequence of jumps through platforms $2, 5, 8, 11, 14$.
statementZhMd:
*在本题中，你将遇到游戏《盗贼之王》的简化模型。*

在 ZeptoLab 推出的一款名为 "King of Thieves" 的新游戏中，你的目标是控制角色，在躲避沿途陷阱和障碍物的同时，到达装有金币的宝箱。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/89ecf94723f2c4b2bbb4ab5e555fd8fca72cbcde.png)

游戏的一个有趣特点是，你可以设计自己的关卡，并将其提供给其他玩家。现在让我们来考虑一种简单的关卡设计。

一个地牢由 $*n*$ 个位于同一水平高度的线段组成，每个线段要么是角色可以站立的平台，要么是一个坑，角色掉进去后会输掉游戏。所有线段的长度都相同，关卡示意图中的平台用 `'*'` 表示，坑用 `'.'` 表示。

影响关卡速通特性的因素之一，是能否进行一系列长度相同的连续跳跃。更正式地说，当角色位于平台 $*i*_{1}$ 上时，如果满足 $*i*_{2} - *i*_{1} = *i*_{3} - *i*_{2} = ... = *i*_{*k*} - *i*_{*k* - 1}$，那么他可以依次跳过平台 $*i*_{1} < *i*_{2} < ... < *i*_{*k*}$。当然，所有线段 $*i*_{1}, *i*_{2}, ... *i*_{*k*}$ 都必须确实是平台，而不能是坑。

如果可以进行长度相同的**四次**跳跃，或者换句话说，存在一个由**五个**平台 $*i*_{1}, *i*_{2}, ..., *i*_{5}$ 组成的序列，且相邻平台之间的距离相同，则称一个关卡是*好的*。给定关卡的示意图，请判断它是否是好的。

## 约束条件

$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$）——关卡中的线段数。

下一行包含一个由 $*n*$ 个字符 `'*'` 和 `'.'` 组成的字符串，表示关卡的示意图。

## 输出格式

如果关卡是*好的*，输出单词 "yes"（不含引号）；否则输出单词 "no"（不含引号）。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，你可以依次跳过平台 $2, 5, 8, 11, 14$。
